nodes.name: Cofinality
nodes.statement: The cofinality $\cof\alpha$ of an ordinal $\alpha$ is $\min\{|A| : A \text{ is an unbounded subset of } \alpha\}$. An infinite cardinal $\lambda$ is regular if $\cof\lambda = \lambda$, otherwise singular.

nodes.name: Strong limit cardinal
nodes.statement: A cardinal $\lambda$ is a limit cardinal if $\mu < \lambda$ implies $\mu^+ < \lambda$, and a strong limit cardinal if $\mu < \lambda$ implies $2^\mu < \lambda$.

nodes.name: Filter and reduced product
nodes.statement: A filter on a set $I$ is a nontrivial collection of subsets of $I$ closed upward under inclusion and under intersection. For an indexed family $\{X_i : i \in I\}$ and filter $\FF$, the reduced product $\prod_i X_i / \FF$ is functions $f \in \prod_i X_i$ modulo $f =_\FF g \iff \{i : f(i)=g(i)\} \in \FF$.

nodes.name: Ultrafilter and ultraproduct
nodes.statement: A maximal nontrivial filter is an ultrafilter; the corresponding reduced product is an ultraproduct. An ultraproduct of linearly ordered sets is again linearly ordered.

nodes.name: Closed-unbounded filter $\FF_\alpha$
nodes.statement: For an ordinal $\alpha$ of uncountable cofinality, $\FF_\alpha$ denotes the filter generated by the closed unbounded subsets of $\alpha$; it is closed under countable intersections.

nodes.name: Possible cofinality
nodes.statement: A cardinal $\lambda$ is a possible cofinality of $\prod \bfa$ (where $\bfa = (\lambda_i)_{i\in I}$ is an indexed set of regular cardinals) if there is an ultrafilter $\FF$ on $I$ for which the cofinality of $\prod \bfa / \FF$ is $\lambda$.

nodes.name: $\pcf \bfa$
nodes.statement: $\pcf \bfa$ is the set of all possible cofinalities of $\prod \bfa$.

nodes.name: True cofinality $\tcf$
nodes.statement: When a product $\prod \bfa / \FF$ contains a cofinal pointwise nondecreasing sequence, its cofinality is called true; we write $\tcf$ for the cofinality in this case.

nodes.name: Pseudopower $\pp_\kappa(\lambda)$
nodes.statement: For $\cof \lambda \le \kappa < \lambda$, $\pp_\kappa(\lambda)$ is the supremum of cofinalities of ultraproducts $\prod \bfa / \FF$ with $\bfa$ a set of at most $\kappa$ regular cardinals below $\lambda$ and $\FF$ an ultrafilter on $\bfa$ containing no set bounded below $\lambda$. $\pp(\lambda) := \pp_{\cof\lambda}(\lambda)$.

nodes.name: $\kappa$-inaccessible cardinal
nodes.statement: $\lambda$ is called $\kappa$-inaccessible if $\mu^\kappa < \lambda$ for all $\mu < \lambda$.

nodes.name: $\PP_\kappa(\lambda)$
nodes.statement: $\PP_\kappa(\lambda)$ is the set of cofinalities whose supremum defines $\pp_\kappa(\lambda)$.

nodes.name: $\kappa$-covering number $\cov(\lambda,\kappa)$
nodes.statement: For $\kappa \in [\cof\lambda, \lambda)$, $\cov(\lambda, \kappa)$ is the minimal cardinality of a family of subsets of $\lambda$, each of size less than $\lambda$, such that every subset of $\lambda$ of size $\kappa$ is contained in one of them.

nodes.name: Weak $\kappa$-covering number
nodes.statement: Minimal cardinality of a family of subsets of $\lambda$, each of size less than $\lambda$, such that every subset of $\lambda$ of size $\kappa$ is contained in the union of countably many of the specified sets.

nodes.name: Index of a cardinal
nodes.statement: If $\kappa = \aleph_\alpha$, the index of $\kappa$ is $\alpha$.

nodes.name: Boolean order algebra of a linear order
nodes.statement: The boolean order algebra associated to a linear order $L$ is the boolean algebra of subsets of $L$ generated by the closed-open intervals.

nodes.name: $\lambda$-narrow Boolean algebra
nodes.statement: A boolean algebra is $\lambda$-narrow if it has no set of pairwise incomparable elements of size $\lambda$ ($a, b$ are incomparable if $a \not\le b$ and $b \not\le a$).

nodes.name: Entangled linear order
nodes.statement: A linear order $L$ is entangled if for every $n$, all distinct $x_{m,i}$ for $m \le n$, $i < |L|$, and any subset $w$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, there exist $i < j$ such that for all $m \le n$, $x_{m,i} < x_{m,j}$ iff $m \in w$.

nodes.name: Jónsson algebra
nodes.statement: A Jónsson algebra is an algebra in a finite or countable language that has no proper subalgebra of the same cardinality.

nodes.name: Theorem A
nodes.statement: If $2^{\aleph_n} < \Ao$ for all $n$, then $2^{\aleph_\omega} < \aleph_{\omega_4}$.

nodes.name: Theorem A'
nodes.statement: $\Ao^{\Az} < \max\{\aleph_{\omega_4}, (\cvt)^+\}$.

nodes.name: Galvin-Hajnal Theorem
nodes.statement: Suppose $\delta$ is a limit ordinal of cofinality $\aleph_1$ and $\Aa^{\aleph_1} < \Ad$ for $\alpha < \delta$. Then $\Ad^{\aleph_1} < \aleph_{(2^{|\delta|})^+}$.

nodes.name: Shelah 111 Theorem on $\lambda^{\aleph_1}$
nodes.statement: If $\lambda > 2^{2^{\aleph_1}}$ satisfies $\mu^{\aleph_1} < \lambda$ for all $\mu < \lambda$, and is below the first regular uncountable limit cardinal, then so is $\lambda^{\aleph_1}$. Similar results hold with $F_1(\alpha) = $ the $\alpha$th fixed point.
assumptions: $\lambda$ below first regular uncountable limit cardinal
conclusions: $\lambda^{\aleph_1}$ is below the first regular uncountable limit cardinal

nodes.name: Theorem B' (4.2)
nodes.statement: If $2^{\Az} < \Ao$ then $\Ao^{\Az} < \aleph_{(\cvt)^+}$.

nodes.name: Main Theorem on pcf structure (4.3)
nodes.statement: Let $\bfa = (\lambda_i)_{i\in I}$ be an indexed set of distinct regular cardinals with each $\lambda \in \bfa$ greater than $|\bfa|$. Then: (1) $|\pcf \bfa| \le 2^{|\bfa|}$; (2) $\pcf \bfa$ has a maximum; (3) $\cof \prod \bfa = \max \pcf \bfa$; (4) for each $\lambda \in \pcf \bfa$ there is $\bfb_\lambda \subseteq \bfa$ with $\lambda = \max \pcf \bfb_\lambda$ and $\lambda \notin \pcf(\bfa - \bfb_\lambda)$; (5) generators $f^\lambda_i$ exist with stated dominance properties.
assumptions: $\bfa$ a set of distinct regular cardinals
conclusions: exact upper bound functions $f^\lambda_i$ exist mod $\JJ_\lambda$

nodes.name: Localization Theorem (4.4)
nodes.statement: Let $\bfa$ be a set of $\kappa$ distinct regular cardinals with $\lambda > \kappa$ for all $\lambda \in \bfa$, and $\bfb \subseteq \pcf \bfa$ with $\lambda > |\bfb|$ for all $\lambda \in \bfb$. If $\mu \in \pcf \bfb$ then $\mu \in \pcf \bfa$, and for some $\bfc \subseteq \bfb$ of cardinality $\le \kappa$, $\mu \in \pcf \bfc$.

nodes.name: Theorem 5.2 (pseudopower bounds)
nodes.statement: (1) $\pp_\kappa(\lambda) \le \lambda^\kappa$. (2) If $\cof\lambda \le \kappa < \lambda < \aleph_\lambda$ and $\lambda$ is $\kappa$-inaccessible, then $\pp_\kappa(\lambda) = \lambda^\kappa$.

nodes.name: Convexity Theorem (5.3)
nodes.statement: If $\kappa \in [\cof\lambda, \lambda)$ then $\PP_\kappa(\lambda)$ is an interval in the set of regular cardinals with minimum element $\lambda^+$.
conclusions: $\PP_\kappa(\lambda)$ is an interval of regular cardinals with minimum $\lambda^+$

nodes.name: First Representation Theorem (5.4)
nodes.statement: Suppose $\Az < \cof\lambda < \kappa < \lambda$ and for all $\mu \in (\kappa, \lambda)$ with $\cof\mu \le \cof\lambda$, $\pp(\mu) < \lambda$. Let $\FF_0$ be the filter on $\cof\lambda$ generated by complements of bounded sets. Then for any regular $\lambda^* \in \PP(\lambda)$, there is an increasing sequence $(\lambda_i)_{i<\cof\lambda}$ with limit $\lambda$ such that $\prod \lambda_i / \FF_0$ has true cofinality $\lambda^*$.
conclusions: There is an increasing sequence $(\lambda_i)_{i<\cof\lambda}$ with $\sup = \lambda$ such that $\prod\lambda_i/\FF_0$ has true cofinality $\lambda^*$

nodes.name: Second Representation Theorem (5.5)
nodes.statement: If $\lambda$ is singular of uncountable cofinality, $\FF_0$ is the filter generated by complements of bounded subsets of $\cof\lambda$, and $(\lambda_i)_{i<\cof\lambda}$ is increasing, continuous, cofinal in $\lambda$, then there is a closed unbounded $C \subseteq \cof\lambda$ such that $\prod_C \lambda_i^+ / \langle\FF_0, \cof\lambda - C\rangle$ has true cofinality $\lambda^+$.
conclusions: There exists a closed unbounded $C \subseteq \cof\lambda$ with $\tcf(\prod_C \lambda_i^+ / \langle\FF_0, \cof\lambda - C\rangle) = \lambda^+$

nodes.name: Theorem 5.7 (pp equals cov)
nodes.statement: If $\kappa \in [\cof\lambda, \lambda)$ and $\lambda < \aleph_\lambda$, then $\pp_\kappa(\lambda)$ equals the $\kappa$-covering number for $\lambda$.

nodes.name: Theorem 5.8 (weak covering)
nodes.statement: (1) For $\kappa$ uncountable, the weak $\kappa$-covering number of $\lambda$ equals the supremum of true cofinalities of reduced products $\prod\bfa/\FF$ with $|\bfa| \le \kappa$ regular cardinals below $\lambda$ and $\FF$ a filter on $\bfa$ closed under countable intersections containing complements of bounded sets. (2) If this cardinal is regular, the supremum is attained.

nodes.name: Theorem 5.9 (covering equals stationary)
nodes.statement: For $\Az < \kappa \le \lambda$ with $\kappa$ regular, the following coincide: (1) the minimal cardinality of a family of subsets of $\lambda$, each of size $< \kappa$, such that any subset of $\lambda$ of cardinality $< \kappa$ is contained in one; (2) the minimal cardinality of a stationary subset of the family of subsets of $\lambda$ of size $< \kappa$.
conclusions: The two minimal cardinalities (1) and (2) are equal

nodes.name: Theorem 6.1 (pp bound on aleph-omega)
nodes.statement: $\pp(\Ao) < \aleph_{\omega_4}$.

nodes.name: Corollary 6.2
nodes.statement: $\Ao^{\Az} < \max(\aleph_{\omega_4}, (\cvt)^+)$.

nodes.name: Theorem 6.3 (general pp bound)
nodes.statement: If $\delta$ is a limit ordinal with $\delta < \aleph_{\alpha+\delta}$, then $\pp(\aleph_{\alpha+\delta}) < \aleph_{\alpha+|\delta|^{+4}}$.

nodes.name: Corollary 7.1 (no resurrection of supercompactness)
nodes.statement: If in $V$ we have $\cof(\lambda) < \kappa < \lambda$ and $\pp(\lambda) > \lambda^+$, then there is no universe extending $V$ in which $\lambda^+$ remains a cardinal while $\kappa$ becomes supercompact or even compact.
conclusions: No extension of $V$ preserves $\lambda^+$ as a cardinal while making $\kappa$ (super)compact

nodes.name: Lemma 7.2 (pp via covering for cofinality $\Az$)
nodes.statement: If $\lambda$ is singular of cofinality $\Az$, $\pp(\mu) < \lambda$ for all singular $\mu < \lambda$ of cofinality $\Az$, and $\pp(\mu) = \mu^+$ for every large enough $\mu < \lambda$ of cofinality $\aleph_1$, then there is a family of $\pp(\lambda)$ countable subsets of $\lambda$ such that every countable subset is contained in one. Hence if $\mu^{\Az} < \lambda$ for all $\mu < \lambda$, $\pp(\lambda) = \lambda^{\Az}$.
assumptions: $\pp(\mu) = \mu^+$ for all sufficiently large $\mu < \lambda$ of cofinality $\aleph_1$
conclusions: A covering family of $\pp(\lambda)$ countable subsets exists

nodes.name: Lemma 7.3 (large pp implies many fixed points)
nodes.statement: If $\lambda$ is singular of cofinality $\Az$, $\mu^{\Az} < \lambda$ for $\mu < \lambda$, and $\pp(\lambda) > \lambda^{\Az}$, then $\pp(\lambda)$ is quite large; there are at least $\aleph_1$ fixed points in $[\lambda^+, \pp(\lambda)]$.
conclusions: At least $\aleph_1$ fixed points (cardinals $\lambda$ with $\lambda = \aleph_\lambda$) lie in $[\lambda^+, \pp(\lambda)]$

nodes.name: Lemma 7.4 (pp equals $\lambda^\kappa$ on club)
nodes.statement: If $\kappa$ is regular uncountable and $(\lambda_i)_{i \le \kappa}$ is increasing continuous with $\lambda_i^\kappa < \lambda_\kappa$ for $i < \kappa$, then for some closed unbounded $C \subseteq \kappa$, $\pp(\lambda_i) = \lambda_i^\kappa$ on $C \cup \{\kappa\}$.
conclusions: There is a closed unbounded $C \subseteq \kappa$ such that $\pp(\lambda_i) = \lambda_i^\kappa$ for all $i \in C \cup \{\kappa\}$

nodes.name: Lemma 8.2 (consequences of strong hypothesis)
nodes.statement: The Strong Hypothesis implies that for any singular $\lambda$ and any $\kappa < \lambda$, $\lambda^\kappa \le \lambda^+ + 2^\kappa$, and there is a covering family of $\lambda^+$ subsets of $\lambda$ each of cardinality $\kappa$; and a Jónsson algebra exists in every successor cardinal.
conclusions: Jónsson algebra exists in every successor cardinal

nodes.name: Lemma 8.4 (consequences of weak hypothesis)
nodes.statement: The Weak Hypothesis implies: $\pp(\Ao) < \aleph_{\omega_1}$, and more generally $\delta < \aleph_\delta \Rightarrow \pp(\aleph_\delta) < \aleph_{|\delta|^+}$; $|\pcf\bfa| \le |\bfa|$; $\pp(\lambda)$ has cofinality $\ge \lambda^+$ for $\lambda$ singular.
assumptions: Weak Hypothesis: for any singular $\lambda$, at most countably many singular $\mu < \lambda$ satisfy $\pp(\mu) \ge \lambda$

nodes.name: Strong Hypothesis (8.1)
nodes.statement: For all singular cardinals $\lambda$, $\pp(\lambda) = \lambda^+$.

nodes.name: Weak Hypothesis (8.3)
nodes.statement: For any singular cardinal $\lambda$, there are at most countably many singular cardinals $\mu < \lambda$ with $\pp(\mu) \ge \lambda$.

nodes.name: Theorem 9.1 (Model Theory)
nodes.statement: If $\lambda$ has cofinality greater than $\aleph_1$, then there are two $L_{\infty,\lambda}$-equivalent nonisomorphic models of cardinality $\lambda$.
conclusions: There exist two $L_{\infty,\lambda}$-equivalent nonisomorphic models of cardinality $\lambda$

nodes.name: Theorem 9.2 (Jónsson algebra at $\aleph_{\omega+1}$)
nodes.statement: There is a Jónsson algebra of cardinality $\aleph_{\omega+1}$.
conclusions: A Jónsson algebra of cardinality $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ exists

nodes.name: Theorem 9.3 (Chain conditions)
nodes.statement: For any cardinal $\lambda > \aleph_1$, there is a Boolean algebra satisfying the $\lambda^+$-chain condition while its square does not; hence its Stone-Čech compactification has cellularity $\lambda$ but its square has cellularity $> \lambda$.
conclusions: There is a Boolean algebra with $\lambda^+$-c.c. whose square fails $\lambda^+$-c.c.
Its Stone-Čech compactification has cellularity $\lambda$ but the square has cellularity $> \lambda$

nodes.name: Coloring Theorem (9.4)
nodes.statement: For $\lambda > \aleph_1$ there is a binary symmetric function $c : (\lambda^+)^2 \to \cof\lambda$ such that for any sequence $(w_i)_{i<\lambda}$ of pairwise disjoint finite subsets of $\lambda^+$ and any $\gamma < \cof\lambda$, there is a pair $i < j < \lambda$ with $c[w_i \times w_j] = \{\gamma\}$.
conclusions: A coloring $c : (\lambda^+)^2 \to \cof\lambda$ exists with the stated rainbow property

nodes.name: Theorem 9.5 (Narrow Boolean algebras)
nodes.statement: (1) If $\lambda$ is singular and less than $\cvt$, then there is a $\lambda^+$-narrow Boolean order algebra of cardinality $\lambda^+$. The same holds if $\kappa^{+3} < \cof\lambda < \lambda < 2^\kappa$. (2) The class $\{\lambda : \text{there is a } \lambda^+\text{-narrow Boolean algebra in } \lambda^+\}$ is unbounded.
conclusions: A $\lambda^+$-narrow Boolean order algebra of cardinality $\lambda^+$ exists
The class is unbounded; in particular $(\lambda, \aleph_{\lambda^{+3}+1}]$ is not disjoint from it

nodes.name: Theorem 9.6 (Almost disjoint sets, almost free abelian groups)
nodes.statement: (1) If $\lambda$ is singular and $\pp(\lambda) > \lambda^+$, then there is a family of $\lambda^+$ subsets of $\lambda$, each of cardinality $\cof\lambda$, with the property that any $\lambda$ of them admit a transversal; consequently if $\cof\lambda = \Az$ there is a $\lambda^+$-free non-free abelian group. (2) For $\lambda > \mu \ge \cvt$, the existence of $\lambda$ subsets of $\mu$ of size $\aleph_1$ with pairwise finite intersection is equivalent to a pcf-condition. (3) If $\lambda$ regular, $2^{<\lambda} < 2^\lambda$, and no linear order of cardinality $2^\lambda$ has density $\lambda$, then in every regular $\mu \in [2^{<\lambda}, 2^\lambda]$ there is an entangled order.
assumptions: For (3): $\lambda$ regular, $2^{<\lambda} < 2^\lambda$, no linear order of cardinality $2^\lambda$ and density $\lambda$
conclusions: (1) Family of $\lambda^+$ subsets with transversal property exists; $\lambda^+$-free non-free abelian group when $\cof\lambda = \aleph_0$
(3) Entangled order exists in every regular $\mu \in [2^{<\lambda}, 2^\lambda]$

nodes.name: Concluding Theorem (cofinality of $S_{\le\Az}(\aleph_{\omega_4})$)
nodes.statement: If $\delta < \aleph_{\omega_4}$ has cofinality $\aleph_0$, then $\pp(\aleph_\delta) < \aleph_{\omega_4}$, and hence the cofinality of the partially ordered set $\langle S_{\le\Az}(\aleph_{\omega_4}); \subseteq\rangle$ is $\aleph_{\omega_4}$, where $S_{\Az}(\lambda) = \{a : a \subseteq \lambda, |a| = \aleph_0\}$.

nodes.name: Monotonicity of $2^\lambda$
nodes.statement: If $\mu \le \lambda$ then $2^\mu \le 2^\lambda$.

nodes.name: König cofinality inequality
nodes.statement: $\cof 2^\lambda > \lambda$.

nodes.name: Product equation (3a)
nodes.statement: $2^{\aleph_\delta} = \prod_{\alpha < \delta} 2^{\aleph_\alpha}$.

nodes.name: Strong limit reduction (3b)
nodes.statement: If $\aleph_\delta$ is a strong limit, $2^{\aleph_\delta} = \aleph_\delta^{\cof\delta}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6.3 (sketched)
nodes.statement: Argument by contradiction: assume $\aleph_{\omega_4+1} \in \pcf(\Ao)$ and analyze the closure operation $\cl$ on $\omega_4$ induced by pcf, then derive a contradiction via the Convexity, Localization, and Second Representation Theorems.

nodes.name: Set up contradiction hypothesis and closure operation
nodes.statement: Assume toward a contradiction that $\aleph_{\omega_4+1} \in \pcf(\Ao)$. For $X \subseteq \omega_4$, define $\cl X = \{i < \omega_4 : \aleph_{i+1} \in \pcf(\aleph_{j+1})_{j \in X}\}$.

nodes.name: Apply Convexity Theorem
nodes.statement: By the Convexity Theorem, $\cl(\omega) = \omega_4$.

nodes.name: Apply Localization Theorem
nodes.statement: By the Localization Theorem, if $i \in \cl X$, then for some countable $Y \subseteq X$, $i \in \cl Y$.

nodes.name: Apply Second Representation Theorem
nodes.statement: By the Second Representation Theorem, if $\delta < \omega_4$ is a limit ordinal of uncountable cofinality, then $\delta$ is the maximal element of $\cl C$ for some closed unbounded subset $C$ of $\delta$ (and any smaller club).

nodes.name: Derive contradiction from incompatible closure properties
nodes.statement: These three properties of the closure operation $\cl$ on $\omega_4$, together with combinatorics of closed unbounded sets in $\omega_4$, are incompatible — no such closure operation can exist on $\omega_4$.
